conditions: Real exponent n and real x strictly positive; special integer cases extend further.
spoken_aliases: the derivative with respect to x of x raised to the power n equals n times x raised to the power of open parenthesis n minus one close parenthesis
d by d x of x to the power n equals n times x to the power of the quantity n minus one end exponent

evidence: For x>0, define x^n=exp(n ln x). Differentiate using the chain rule: exp(n ln x)n/x=nx^(n-1). This proof includes n=0 since x is strictly positive.

Reference cross-check: https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-1/pages/3-3-differentiation-rules; https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-1/pages/3-9-derivatives-of-exponential-and-logarithmic-functions. Checked 2026-11-27. Proposed maintainer approval; not independent human certification.
